lesson.title: Trap Watch: False Friends in the Wild
lesson.subtitle: High-frequency false friends (actuellement, librairie, attendre, raisin, journée, location) in context.

hook.title: Trap Watch: Outsmarting the Full False-Friends Deck in Context
hook.content: Alongside actuellement ('currently'), la librairie ('bookshop'), attendre ('to wait for'), and demander ('to ask'), watch out for four more classic traps: le raisin ('fresh grape' — a dried raisin is un raisin sec!), la journée ('the day' — Bonne journée ! is 'Have a good day!'), la location ('rental/lease'), and formidable ('wonderful/tremendous')!

footnotes.title: Why 'Bonne journée !' means 'Have a good day!' and not 'Have a good trip!'
footnotes.content: jour ('day') + -née ('the span of') = la journée ('the whole day long'). A travel journey is un voyage!

pattern.title: Read the French Meaning, Ignore the English Lookalike
pattern.content: Test yourself across the false friends in live context.
pattern.linguist_note: Semantic divergence creates false cognates between sibling lexicons.
pattern.trap_note: Never wish someone *Bonne journée when you mean 'Have a safe trip' (that's Bon voyage !)!

exercises.prompt: Match each French false friend with its TRUE French meaning:
exercises.target_answer: fresh grape (not dried raisin), the day's span (not travel journey), rental / lease (not geographic location), wonderful / terrific (not fearsome), bookshop (not lending library), currently (not actually)
exercises.meaning: le raisin (vs. un raisin sec), la journée (Bonne journée !), la location (voiture de location), formidable (C'est formidable !), la librairie (vs. la bibliothèque), actuellement (vs. vraiment / en fait)
exercises.explanation: Every one of these words kept its spelling while shifting meaning on one side of the Channel.

exercises.prompt: What does 'C'est une voiture de location' mean?
options: It is a car in this location
exercises.meaning: la location = rental / lease (from louer 'to rent')
exercises.explanation: Geographic location is le lieu or l'endroit; la location is a rental!

exercises.prompt: Which English sentences accurately translate 'Ton idée est formidable, bonne journée'?
exercises.german: Ton idée est formidable, bonne journée
exercises.meaning: Your idea is wonderful, have a great day!
renderings: Your idea is wonderful, have a good day!
Your idea is terrific, have a nice day!
traps: Your idea is terrifying, have a safe trip!
Your idea is formidable, good journey!
exercises.target_answer: Your idea is wonderful, have a good day!
exercises.explanation: formidable means 'wonderful/terrific', and bonne journée means 'have a good day'.

exercises.idea: I am waiting for my friend in front of the bookshop (use devant la librairie)
cues: I wait-for my friend → J'attends mon ami
in front of the bookshop → devant la librairie
idea_parts: verb + direct object → J'attends mon ami
exercises.target_answer: J'attends mon ami devant la librairie
exercises.meaning: I am waiting for my friend in front of the bookshop
exercises.explanation: Combines attendre ('wait for') and la librairie ('bookshop').

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: J'habite actuellement ici et c'est formidable
exercises.target_answer: J'habite actuellement ici et c'est formidable
exercises.meaning: I currently live here and it is wonderful
exercises.affirmation: You decoded both false friends in one sentence!

summary.outcome: Spot and accurately use French false friends in context.

use_example.english: Thank you very much and have a great day!

summary.takeaway: la journée = the day; le raisin = fresh grape; la location = rental; formidable = wonderful.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "I am waiting for my friend in front of the bookshop" in French:
twist.target_answer: J'attends mon ami devant la librairie
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "J'attends mon ami devant la librairie" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of Trap Watch: False Friends in the Wild.

trap_actuellement.context_translation: I currently live in Lyon. (NOT English "actually")
trap_actuellement.etymology_derivation: actuellement is time, not truth: 'je travaille actuellement à Paris' = 'I'm currently working in Paris'. The actually you want is en fait (in fact).

trap_librairie.context_phrase: J'achète des livres à la librairie.
trap_librairie.context_translation: I buy books at the bookshop. (NOT English "library")
trap_librairie.etymology_derivation: the librairie sells books. The lending library is la bibliothèque.

trap_attendre.context_translation: I'm waiting for the bus. (NOT English "to attend")
trap_attendre.etymology_derivation: j'attends le train = I'm waiting for the train. Attending a class is suivre (to follow) un cours.

trap_demander.context_translation: I'm going to ask for directions. (NOT English "to demand")
trap_demander.etymology_derivation: demander is the everyday 'to ask' — no aggression inside. Demanding is exiger.

trap_raisin.etymology_derivation: le raisin is a fresh grape on the vine (and produces le vin). A dried raisin is un raisin sec ('a dry grape').

trap_journée.context_translation: Have a great day, everyone! (NOT English "journey")
trap_journée.etymology_derivation: Bonne journée ! means 'Have a good day!', not 'Have a good trip!'. A travel journey is un voyage.

trap_location.etymology_derivation: une voiture de location is a rental car. A geographic location or spot is un lieu or un endroit.

trap_formidable.etymology_derivation: In modern French, C'est formidable ! is high praise ('That's wonderful!'), with zero fear attached.
